sections.html:
Up in the northwest corner of Arkansas, Bentonville serves as the Benton County seat, bordered by Rogers, Bella Vista and Centerton. Its population went from 19,730 in 2000 to 35,301 in 2010 and 54,164 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate stands at 63,057. Housing units numbered 22,436 in 2020, and 8.7 percent stood vacant.

Walmart anchors the local economy, with a Home Office campus along Walton Boulevard (US 71B). A consolidated headquarters on about 350 acres was announced in 2017, and the first part opened in January 2025. More than 1,100 vendors keep sales offices nearby. Relocation timing drives many sales here: an employee transferring on a company schedule often cannot sit through a long listing.

Most of the city belongs to Bentonville Public Schools, whose high schools are Bentonville High School and Bentonville West High School, the latter in Centerton. Rogers Public Schools zone a few small eastern pockets. Haas Hall Academy and Founders Classical Academy are public charter options, and the Thaden School is independent. Zones can change from one street to the next, so verify yours before you describe the house to anyone.

sections.h2: Weather, ground and what inspectors check
sections.html:
Four distinct seasons shape the housing stock. Summer highs average 89 degrees in July, winter lows reach 24 in January, and snowfall adds up to 9.5 inches against about 47 inches of total precipitation. Cold weather puts stress on heating and pipes.

The county sits on the Springfield Plateau, a karst area with springs, sinkholes and caves, so drainage and ground conditions deserve a look.

  • Roof age and storm damage.
  • Foundation movement and drainage on sloped lots.
  • Furnace and heat pump condition after cold stretches.
  • Sinkhole or ground-settlement signs on karst terrain.

Collection in Benton County follows a fixed calendar, and taxes run one year behind. A 2026 assessment is billed in 2027 and due October 15, 2027. Anything unpaid after October 15 takes a 10 percent penalty.

sections.h2: How a sale changes the assessment
sections.html:
A sold house is assessed at 20 percent of appraised value on the next assessment date after title transfers. The buyer waits until the second assessment date after the transfer before any assessed-value limitation applies. The county's next countywide reappraisal is 2028.

A primary residence can carry a homestead credit of up to $600, and the assessor's homestead department answers at 479-271-1037. The bill goes to whoever is owner of record on January 1 of the tax year, and your closing documents lay out how you and the buyer divide it.

Paying the collector by card adds a provider's convenience fee: $3.99 at minimum for payments under $110, and 3.59 percent above that. The state's transfer tax is $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration on transfers over $100.

The Fire Department's Building and Fire Safety Division, at 305 SW A Street, handles permits for building, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, moving, demolition, signs, pools, fire alarms, fire sprinklers and fences. After final inspection it issues certificates of occupancy, and it inspects substandard buildings too. Call 479-271-3108 or write to buildingpermits@bentonville.ar.gov on weekdays between 8 a.m. and 4:30 p.m.

Unpermitted work or an older structure with loose ends is worth a question to the division before you list. More than 30 properties in the city are on the National Register of Historic Places, two of them historic districts, and a house near the square may fall inside one. That status can limit what repairs and exterior changes a buyer can practically make.

sections.h2: Preparing the house and the paperwork
sections.html:
Before you talk price with anyone, gather the deed, your last tax statement and any permit records. Walk the lot for drainage trouble, especially on a slope, and note the age of the roof and the heating system. A buyer on karst terrain may ask whether anyone has noticed settlement, so answer honestly and keep any reports.

If your house is old enough to sit near the square, call the Building and Fire Safety Division and ask about the property record. A short answer now prevents a delay after you have a contract. Heirs and out-of-town owners can usually sort most of this by phone and email. Keep copies of everything you send so you can answer a buyer's question the same day.

sections.h2: What a title search can turn up
sections.html:
The search covers more than taxes. It looks for liens, unreleased claims and any recorded document that clouds title. If something shows up, the closing agent tells you what has to be cleared and whether it can be paid from the proceeds.

Old permits that were never closed out are a common surprise in older neighborhoods. A call to the Building and Fire Safety Division before you list lets you fix the paperwork while there is no deadline pressure. Sellers who handle it early usually reach closing on the date they planned. When a buyer pays cash there is no lender asking for extra documents, but the title company still needs the same clean record, so do not skip the early calls.

If the house has been in the family for years, also confirm who is on the deed. Missing signatures are the quickest way to stall a closing.

Interstate 49 carries US 71 through town, and the Bella Vista Bypass to the north opened in late 2021. Northwest Arkansas National Airport is about 12 miles southwest. With more than 50 miles of trails in the city, how close your house is to one is easy for a buyer to check.

Sellers in Bentonville come with different pressures: a job move, an inheritance, a failed rental or a house that needs work. Whatever the reason, a listing still means repairs, showings and an appraisal for the buyer's loan.

A cash sale is a different route, with one buyer, no financing contingency and a date you choose. Measure it against a listing by your net after repairs and carrying costs, and have any offer in writing before you decide.

The title company starts by searching the Benton County record for unpaid tax, liens and recorded problems. Hand over your last tax statement, deed and permit paperwork. Keep your reappraisal notice, since the buyer's assessment starts only after title transfers.

You sign the deed, and what you owe comes out of the proceeds. Decide who covers recording and transfer tax costs, and write it into the contract.

faqs.q: Is Bentonville the county seat of Benton County?
faqs.a: Yes. Yes, and the 19th Judicial Circuit Court meets in the Benton County Courthouse. Deeds for Bentonville houses are recorded there.

faqs.q: When are Benton County property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 15, followed by a 10 percent penalty. The books open the first business day of March, and billing runs one year behind the assessment.

faqs.q: How does a sale change my property tax assessment in Bentonville?
faqs.a: It is assessed at 20 percent of appraised value at the next assessment date after the title transfers, and the new owner has to wait until the second assessment date for any assessed-value limitation.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate of occupancy to sell?
faqs.a: The Building and Fire Safety Division issues them after construction and final inspection. If you are unsure about past work, call 479-271-3108.

faqs.q: Which district is my Bentonville house in?
faqs.a: Most of the city is Bentonville Public Schools, with a few eastern areas zoned to Rogers. Check your street.
